question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a frozen multi-host pool confirmed during DESIGN by a pre-freeze attainability certificate to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state-carrying items on at least two distinct hosts/engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine) via the frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth<=6, budget 250), what fraction of those DEEP items is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (one discovery GET + item-page GET + one spare) using ANY of the five frozen discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) - with the preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 engines deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistent path caching is not the optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface?
hypothesis: Site-native discovery channels (robots.txt/sitemap directives, sitemap.xml, on-site search, RSS/Atom feeds, JSON-LD structured data) enable a fresh agent to reach DEEP (hop>=3) state items in O(1) GETs (K<=3) on at least two distinct engines, demonstrating that shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier. If true, persistent path caching is not the primary optimization target and effort should shift to discovery-channel procedure caching and substrate expansion. If false, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface.
falsifier: Two-sided, arithmetically checkable before freeze, satisfiable in BOTH directions. Let D_e be the set of confirmed DEEP items on engine e, and R_e ⊆ D_e the subset reachable in <=K=3 GETs via ANY frozen discovery channel. Primary metric: discovery_reachable_fraction_e = |R_e| / |D_e| for each engine e with |D_e| >= 3. Decision rule: if discovery_reachable_fraction_e >= 0.50 for at least two distinct engines e, then verdict = FLAT (hop is NOT a fundamental barrier); else verdict = GROWING (fresh acquisition remains path-bound). Both branches are arithmetically reachable because the pre-freeze attainability certificate guarantees |D_e| >= 3 for >=2 engines (denominator > 0) and the positive control guarantees at least one reachable item exists (numerator can be > 0), while the negative/null controls guarantee the numerator can be < denominator.

baselines.description: Fresh agent with NO discovery channels; only direct URL access if URL is known a priori. Expected: 0% reachability for DEEP items (URL unknown), 100% for NEAR items if URL provided. Measures the null cost of zero knowledge.

Link-following BFS on same-host static <a href> graph (frozen policy: depth<=6, budget 250, document order). Cost = hop+1 GETs per item. This is the path-bound comparator from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378. Expected: 100% reachability for admitted DEEP items at cost = hop+1 GETs.

Discovery channel assignment shuffled across items (null control). Measures chance reachability without semantic alignment between discovery channel and item. Expected: near-zero reachability for DEEP items.

positive_control.description: A DEEP item confirmed during DESIGN to be reachable in <=K=3 GETs via at least one frozen discovery channel on at least one engine. Verified by live probe during pre-freeze attainability certificate construction. Must PASS (reachable) for freeze to proceed.

null_control.description: A synthetic item URL known not to exist on any target host (e.g., /__spider_nonexistent_38085197666__.html). Discovery channels must NOT report it as reachable. Must PASS (not reachable) for freeze to proceed.

measurement_validity.substrate: credential-free GET-only Python stdlib HTTP (urllib), TLS verified, User-Agent 'SPIDER-frontier-38085197666/1.0', timeout 15s, max body 1MB, redirects followed, no browser/Docker/model/credentials/cookies/write verbs
measurement_validity.hop_confirmation: Frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth<=6, budget 250, document order, exact hostname equality) executed during DESIGN to confirm DEEP (hop>=3) items. Identical to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 structural crawl policy.

discovery_channels.ROBOTS_SITEMAP: Fetch robots.txt, extract Sitemap: directives, fetch and parse referenced sitemaps (XML, .gz) for URLs matching state-item patterns
discovery_channels.SITEMAP_XML: Fetch /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap.gz; parse urlset/url/loc entries; filter for state-item URL patterns
discovery_channels.ON_SITE_SEARCH: Identify site search endpoint (via <form>, /search, /query, OpenSearch); issue queries derived from known state-item identifiers; parse result URLs
discovery_channels.RSS_ATOM: Fetch /feed, /rss, /atom.xml, /rss.xml; parse item/link/guid entries; filter for state-item URL patterns
discovery_channels.JSON_LD: Fetch homepage and key section pages; extract <script type='application/ld+json'>; parse @graph/@id/url for state-item identifiers

measurement_validity.k_get_breakdown: 1 discovery GET (channel fetch) + 1 item-page GET + 1 spare (redirect/validation)

pre_freeze_attainability_certificate.freeze_gate: Freeze proceeds ONLY if all certificate items are verified and recorded in spec.json with evidence refs

representation_losses: Static HTML parser only (stdlib html.parser); JavaScript-rendered links/controls missed
No authentication/session/cookie handling; private/gated content inaccessible
robots.txt compliance: discovery channels respect Disallow but crawl policy follows same-host <a> only
Sitemap.gz decompression via stdlib gzip; parsing errors cause channel skip for that sitemap
On-site search requires identifiable query parameter; sites without search or with opaque JS search are channel-unavailable
JSON-LD limited to inline <script type='application/ld+json'>; external references not followed

decision_rule.satisfiability_justification: Pre-freeze certificate guarantees denominator > 0 (|D_e| >= 3 for >=2 engines). Positive control guarantees numerator CAN be > 0. Negative/null controls guarantee numerator CAN be < denominator. The 0.50 threshold is strictly between 0 and 1.

product_consequence_positive: If FLAT: shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier. Persistent path/procedure caching is not the primary optimization target. Effort moves to: (1) discovery-channel procedure caching (canonicalize and cache discovery queries/results), (2) substrate expansion (POST, auth, JS rendering, WebSocket), (3) cross-episode discovery freshness/invalidation. The product architecture shifts from path-persistence to discovery-persistence.
product_consequence_negative: If GROWING: fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound even with site-native discovery. Persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface. The product must invest in: (1) path/procedure persistence with freshness guards, (2) delta repair for local Web changes, (3) break-even reuse counting from real re-derivation costs. The current Graph/Physics emphasis on path caching is validated.

estimated_cost.http_gets_design_phase: ~500 (hop confirmation crawl + discovery channel probes + controls)
estimated_cost.http_gets_execute_phase: ~2000 (2 sessions x ~10 seeds x 250 budget + discovery probes + controls)
estimated_cost.compute: single CPU, no GPU, no model calls
estimated_cost.external_dependencies: public HTTP endpoints only; no API keys

expected_information_gain: High. This is the first measurement of site-native discovery reachability vs. hop depth on a multi-engine DEEP pool. The v1 freeze (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) committed an empty sampling frame (0 seeds, 0 DEEP, 0 hosts) so the question is entirely unmeasured. Either outcome changes a central architectural decision (path-persistence vs. discovery-persistence).

freeze_eligibility.decision_rule_reachability_justification: The two-sided decision rule is arithmetically checkable before freeze. The pre-freeze attainability certificate guarantees denominator > 0 (|D_e| >= 3 for >=2 engines) and the positive/negative/null controls guarantee both numerator > 0 and numerator < denominator are possible. The 0.50 threshold is strictly interior to [0,1]. Both FLAT and GROWING branches are reachable.
freeze_eligibility.measurement_prerequisites_justification: All prerequisites are executable during DESIGN: (1) candidate seed curation, (2) frozen same-host BFS hop-confirmation crawl (stdlib HTTP, budget 250, depth 6), (3) discovery channel probing per engine, (4) positive/negative/null control verification, (5) prereg section 18 design decisions resolution. No unavailable substrate, model, dataset, or tool is required. The substrate (credential-free GET-only stdlib HTTP) was environment-verified viable in EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 and EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167.
freeze_eligibility.baseline_identifiability_justification: Three distinct baselines with non-overlapping cost profiles: COLD_BASELINE (0% DEEP reachability, 1 GET if URL known), SHORTEST_PATH_BASELINE (100% DEEP reachability at cost hop+1 GETs), RANDOM_DISCOVERY_BASELINE (near-0% DEEP reachability). The treatment (DISCOVERY_TREATMENT) uses a fundamentally different acquisition mechanism (site-native discovery channels) with a fixed K=3 GET budget independent of hop. The cost signatures are disjoint: COLD=0/1, SHORTEST_PATH=hop+1, DISCOVERY<=3, RANDOM≈0.
freeze_eligibility.control_sensitivity_justification: Five controls with independent pass/fail criteria verified during DESIGN: (1) POS_DISCOVERY_REACHABLE must be reachable in <=3 GETs via discovery (fires if discovery works), (2) NEG_DISCOVERY_UNREACHABLE must NOT be reachable (fires if false positives exist), (3) CALIBRATION_NEAR: NEAR (hop<=1) items should have high discovery reachability (fires if discovery systematically fails), (4) CALIBRATION_DEEP_LINK: DEEP items reachable via link-following BFS at cost hop+1 (fires if hop confirmation is wrong), (5) RANDOM_DISCOVERY_BASELINE: permuted channel assignment should yield near-zero reachability. All controls are executable during DESIGN and their pass/fail is recorded in the pre-freeze certificate.
freeze_eligibility.treatment_liveness_justification: The treatment (site-native discovery channels) is a pure stdlib-HTTP procedure: fetch robots.txt/sitemap.xml/search/RSS/JSON-LD, parse for URLs, fetch candidate item pages. No browser, model, credential, or write verb required. The positive control verified during DESIGN demonstrates the treatment CAN produce a reachable result. The treatment code path is distinct from baselines and will be exercised in EXECUTE. The treatment is not structurally incapable of becoming EXECUTABLE.
freeze_eligibility.freeze_artifacts_bound_justification: All mutable local interpretation dependencies are enumerated in freeze_artifacts below with repository-relative paths. The deterministic freezer will hash them into freeze.json.artifact_hashes. No external mutable dependencies (datasets, model weights, API endpoints) exist beyond the public HTTP targets which are fixed by the frozen candidate seed list.
